v4.9.077 - the pictures stop blinking (#360)

#360 Roman: "a short flashing of all content after each sync… it's distracting."
     He assumed the sync was reloading everything. The sync was innocent; it only
     triggers the redraw that showed the fault.

     TWO CAUSES, and the first one is the big one:

     A main frame holding a picture is not drawn on a canvas at all - it is a
     plain picture element, and every one of them carried loading="lazy". So the
     browser had been told it may put off fetching that picture until it feels
     like it. Every redraw threw those elements away and made new ones, and every
     picture on screen was asked for again, lazily. That is the flash, in every
     view - strips, 3x2, M+2, M+3 - and under the scribble layer too, which has
     no pictures of its own and was simply sitting on top of one that blanked.
     They are no longer lazy, and are decoded before being shown rather than
     after.

     The canvases had their own version of the same mistake. Every picture was
     decoded from scratch each time: the canvas was wiped immediately and painted
     only once the picture had decoded. A picture is now decoded once and kept,
     so a card is painted the instant it is built. Only a picture this device has
     never shown still waits - and then the canvas is left alone until it is
     ready, rather than being wiped first.

     The store already holds every picture in the project, so what is kept here
     is the decoded copy, not a second copy of the data. 150 of them, oldest out.

A TEST THAT CAN SEE A FLASH

It puts a picture on a card, then watches that card twenty-five times a second
for twelve seconds while the other device works, and fails if the card is ever
caught showing nothing. It handles both kinds - the canvas and the picture
element.

Honest note: unlike the other new tests, this one has never failed for me, so its
teeth are unproven. It WOULD catch the lazy pictures - a fresh lazy element
reports itself as not loaded, which is exactly what it looks for - but I did not
back the fix out to prove it.

Three wrong turns getting there, all mine, all found by the test rather than by
Roman: a base64 picture I typed from memory that was not a valid picture at all;
an on-screen check that rejects anything inside a fixed container, which is how
the grid sits; and putting the picture on a version while the card was showing
the main frame.

20 of 20 pass.
